title: TESS data show transits at the radial-velocity period of TOI-1117 c and exclude most transits of 423 other radial-velocity planets with periods up to 100 days
abstract: Question: do TESS 2-minute light curves show transits at the known periods of planets that radial-velocity (RV) surveys found, and where do the data exclude transits? Method: we searched the light curves (sectors 1-107, 2018-2026) of 448 RV planets with P <= 100 d on 332 hosts. We used a phase-binned box statistic near each RV period, the RV conjunction prior when available, control periods, and an exclusion test calibrated with 4,230 injected transits (1 false exclusion in 3,983 covered injections). Results: (1) TOI-1117 c, which the discovery paper classified as non-transiting, shows a 471 +- 52 ppm, 1.9 h dip at P = 4.578646 +- 0.000035 d, equal to the RV period (4.579 +- 0.004 d). The dip is consistent in all 2-minute sectors, in odd and even events and in SAP flux, and the centroid does not move. 0 of 2,000 random periods reach its SNR. Sector 13 (2019) data that we did not use in the search show the dip at the predicted times in three pipelines (440-685 ppm; p < 0.001 each). The implied radius is about 2.5 Earth radii. We call it a strong transit candidate, not a confirmed transit. (2) For 324 of 423 non-transiting RV planets, the data exclude at 3 sigma at least 90% of the RV-prior conjunction probability for transits of half or more of the predicted depth (b < 0.87). (3) In 381 RV-selected planets, geometry predicts 19.8 transiting planets and the search recovers the 16 known ones (p = 0.22). (4) The other 11 screened signals are systematics, blends, or the known synchronized spot modulation of HD 41004 B. Limitations: predicted depths use mass-radius estimates; grazing transits are not tested; TOI-1117 c needs a dedicated transit observation and a joint fit.

display.caption: TOI-1117 c transit candidate. Top left: TESS 2-minute data (sectors 39 and 100-103), TOI-1117 b masked, folded at P = 4.57865 d, with the trapezoid fit. Top right: box depth per sector; green points are sector 13 full-frame-image data from three pipelines, not used in the search or the fit. Bottom left: sector 13 TESS-SPOC data at the predicted times. Bottom right: maximum box SNR of the same search at 2,000 random periods (grey) and at the RV period (red).

Excluded fraction of the RV-prior conjunction probability for transits of 0.5 x the predicted depth or more (b < 0.87), against RV period. The colour gives the predicted depth. Red stars are the known transiting RV planets; their true transit phases are not excluded, so their fractions are low. Right: histogram for 0.5 x and 0.25 x the predicted depth.

Maximum box SNR at the RV period against the maximum SNR at four control periods. Non-transiting planets follow the 1:1 line; known transiting planets lie far above it. TOI-1117 c and HD 41004 B b are marked.

citations.reason: Discovery paper of the TOI-1117 system. It classified TOI-1117 c as non-transiting from TESS sectors 13 and 39. We report transit evidence at its RV period, mainly from sectors 100-103, and we use its RV period and mass.
Reported the 31-hour TESS modulation of HD 41004 and attributed it to the synchronized M dwarf. We recover it in 7 sectors from 2018 to 2025 and measure its phase against the RV ephemeris.
Discovery of the 1.3-day brown dwarf companion HD 41004 B b; orbit used for the phase test.
